name: The Lowden household at 1912 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_lowden_frank_orren

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1912 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1912 Mr. & Mrs. Frank Orren Lowden.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1912, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The twelve live-in staff and two children it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. A coachman's wife and children in the rear building are named in his note rather than carded. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Frank Orren Lowden

occupation.note: He 'practiced law in Chicago for about 20 years', and from 1904 to 1912 sat on the Republican National Committee (Wikipedia); later governor of Illinois.

persons.note: The 1900 census lists F. O. Lowden here as head, born April 1864 (the figures are hard to read), in Iowa (as read), married, lawyer (ED 40, sheet 4B, line 77, leaf n801).

persons.name: Florence Pullman Lowden
persons.note: The Blue Book prints her as Mrs. Frank Orren Lowden; Wikipedia names her Florence, the daughter of George Pullman, whose widow lived across the street at 1729. The 1900 census lists Florence P. Lowden here as wife, born August 1868 (the figures are hard to read), in Illinois, married (ED 40, sheet 4B, line 78, leaf n801).
